title: Most Enterprise Agentic Projects Are Doomed, Here's Why — Jess Grogan-Avignon & Jack Wang, Accenture
talk_summary: Accenture consultants describe five 'enterprise tensions' (speed, value, delivery, trust, moat) that doom agentic projects, mostly organizational: human-speed governance, business-case certainty, feature-milestone planning, and one-shot deployment. The only concrete, copyable mechanisms are progressive-autonomy rollout (shadow → advisory → controlled autonomy, gated by outcome evidence) and hypothesis-driven build/evaluate/iterate loops instead of fixed milestones.

takeaways.what_they_do: Deploy agents in shadow mode (run alongside humans, cannot affect outcomes), compare agent decisions to human decisions as an iteration signal, then advisory mode (recommend only, human approves/rejects), then controlled autonomy in narrow low-risk scenarios with kill switches, expanding only as outcome evidence accumulates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you start with a shadow mode where an agent might run alongside human processes, but it can't actually affect outcomes

takeaways.technique: Evidence-gated promotion, not pass/fail or activity completion
takeaways.what_they_do: Each autonomy step is gated by confidence in outcomes on live behavior, explicitly not by project-plan completion or pass-fail test suites; eval suites must measure the right behaviors because agent behavior is emergent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each step is gated by evidence in outcomes. It's not based on completion of activities in a project plan or pass-fail testing

takeaways.technique: Hypothesis-driven small loops instead of milestone plans
takeaways.what_they_do: Reshape delivery around one goal — building statistical confidence — via small build/evaluate/iterate loops producing fast evidence, because non-deterministic agent behavior can't be scoped or milestoned like a feature build.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Small loops of build, evaluate, iterate, fast evidence.

takeaways.technique: Automate human process gates as executable code
takeaways.what_they_do: Every human approval/sign-off step should become executable code (CI/CD-style automation) rather than meetings or review chains, since approval infrastructure is the bottleneck once code supply explodes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every single human process needs to become adaptable, executable code. Not another meeting, not a sign-off chain, code.
takeaways.numbers: GitHub: ~275M commits/week in 2025, on track for 14B/year

takeaways.technique: Feedback signal as the durable asset
takeaways.what_they_do: Require every shipped feature to either generate a feedback signal or act on one already collected, treating customer-edge-case/behavior data ('living memory') as the only non-copyable moat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every feature you ship should either generate that feedback signal or deliver on what the signal has already taught you.
